C0134.title: Sega In-Game Currency Fraud Case: Multiple Parties Found Guilty of Computer-Use Fraud
C0134.summary: In August 2024, multiple parties involved in Sega's game apps were arrested on suspicion of computer-use fraud (using computers to defraud) and subsequently received guilty verdicts. A criminal group advertised a 'top-up proxy' service on RMT sites, sending fraudulent payment information to Sega's servers to illicitly obtain in-game currency, then resold it on RMT sites below the official price. Users who commissioned the top-up proxy were also arrested, prosecuted, and found guilty. Sega issued a statement warning players against participating in such illegal top-up schemes.
